correctness.rationale: For the regular simplex represented by coordinate vertices in the zero-sum subspace H_N, directional width is max u_i−min u_i. Any normalized direction with an intermediate coordinate can strictly decrease width by shifting that coordinate away from its mean while retaining range, so a local minimum must be two-level. A cut of size t yields width sqrt(N/[t(N−t)]). The tangent to a two-level normal has zero sums within both cut blocks; for angles θ<arctan(w/√2) cross-block order is fixed. Sharp zero-sum block bounds ||x||²≤r(r−1)(max x)² imply min over unit tangent v of max_high v−min_low v is 1/sqrt(max{t(t−1),s(s−1)}), attained by the one-exception vector in the larger block. Therefore exact finite-angle envelope is w cosθ+γ sinθ, giving strict local minima, and no others. An independent 7,329 integer zero-sum block probes and 4 partitions with 500 angular probes each corroborated the closed bound, not extrapolation. N≥3, oriented antipodes counted separately, open angle cutoff only.
